chunks: From him, from Moalla, from Ahmad ibn Gassan, from Sama'at who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so he said to me initiating: O Sama'at! What is this which is between you and your camelier? Beware of becoming immoral, or vociferous, or cursing! So I said, By Allah! That was so because he had been unjust to me. So he said: If he has been unjust to you, so you have profited upon him. This is not from my deeds nor do I order my Shias with it. Seek Forgiveness of your Lord and do not repeat. I said, I seek Forgiveness of Allah and I shall not repeat.

key_terms.أَرْبَيْتَ عَلَيْهِ: you profited/gained advantage over him (compensation for his fault)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq teach about responding to injustice with cursing?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Shia emphasis on dignified conduct (adab) even in moments of grievance, distinguishing between the right to compensation (ribh) and the spiritual cost of excessive cursing (lana). Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) uses this incident to correct Sama'at, teaching that while injustice justifies redress, uncontrolled vociferation and obscenity are not characteristic of the Ahl al-Bayt's followers. The narrative serves as a practical guide for maintaining spiritual purity and avoiding the 'excesses' of emotion that detract from one's religious identity.

en.hubeali: From him, from Moalla, from Ahmad Bin Gassan, from Sama’at who said,

‘I went over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said to me initiating: O Sama’at! What is this which is between you and your camelier?’ Beware of becoming immoral, or vociferous, or cursing!’ So I said, ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! That was so because he had been unjust to me’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If he has been unjust to you, so you have profited upon him. This is not from my<sup>asws</sup> deeds nor do I<sup>asws</sup> order my<sup>asws</sup> Shias with it. Seek Forgiveness of your Lord<sup>azwj</sup> and do not repeat’. I said, ‘I seek Forgiveness of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and I shall not repeat’’.
en.sarwar: 14. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Mu’alla from Ahmad ibn Ghassan from Sama’a who has said the following:

“Once I went to see abu ‘Abd Allah, recipient of divine supreme covenant. The Imam on his own initiation said to me, ‘O Sama’a, what was that between you and your camel man? Beware of becoming abusive, loud and using foul language.’ I (the narrator) then said, ‘By Allah, it happened but he did injustice to me.’ The Imam said, ‘If he has done injustice to you, you have gained over him. This is not among my behaviors and I do not command my Shi’a (followers) to behave as such. Ask forgiveness from your Lord and do not repeat.’ I then said, ‘I ask forgiveness from Allah and I will not repeat.’”
